_readme: Record-based source of truth for the Lightning (SFX) EmailTemplate 'IR Offering Notification Email'. Loaded by scripts/apex/investor-relations/load-lightning-email-templates.apex via idempotent upsert-by-DeveloperName DML (NOT Metadata API deploy) -- same pattern as the other two templates in that folder. This file is the human-readable/diffable copy of the scalar fields the loader writes; the loader embeds its own copies directly in Apex (Apex cannot read files at runtime), so if you change a value here, update the loader to match. The HTML body lives alongside this file in IR_Offering_Notification_Email.html and is embedded in the loader as base64 -- regenerate that blob if the .html changes.
Name: IR Offering Notification Email
Subject: New Offering awaiting review: %%RECORDNAME%%
Description: Lightning (SFX) notification for Offering Queue members. Sent by IR_Offering_Notification_Flow via the OfferingEmailSender Apex invocable, which looks this record up by DeveloperName and substitutes the %%RECORDNAME%%, %%RECORDID%%, %%BASEURL%% and %%FIRSTNAME%% tokens. This record IS the live body - editing this file and re-running the loader changes what recipients receive.
_THIS_TEMPLATE_IS_THE_LIVE_SEND_PATH: READ THIS BEFORE EDITING. This record is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what Offering Queue members actually receive. IR_Offering_Notification_Flow holds no copy of the subject or body: it passes only the DeveloperName IR_Offering_Notification_Email to the OfferingEmailSender Apex invocable, which queries this record at run time and merges the %%...%% tokens. CONSEQUENCE: to change the wording, edit the sibling .html (and the Subject in the loader), re-run scripts/apex/investor-relations/load-lightning-email-templates.apex, and the change is live - no flow edit, no Apex deploy. PORTABILITY: this is also what lets the codebase deploy to a new org with nothing built by hand - deploy the metadata, run the loader, done.
_tokens_used_by_this_body: The subject carries %%RECORDNAME%%. The body carries %%RECORDNAME%% (headline), %%FIRSTNAME%% (greeting) and %%BASEURL%%/%%RECORDID%% (the Review Offering button). OfferingEmailSender merges the record tokens once per send and %%FIRSTNAME%% once per recipient. Do NOT use the platform {{{...}}} merge syntax here: it is resolved by the send pipeline, which is the same pipeline that refuses to supply a record context on a User-targeted send - see the next key. The sibling Lead and Welcome templates DO use {{{...}}} because they go out through the standard Send Email action, not through this class.
_html_authoring_constraints: Same rules as the sibling templates. (1) TABLES ONLY for layout and EVERY style INLINE -- Outlook renders with the Word engine and Gmail strips <style> blocks from <head>. (2) NO external images, webfonts or CSS -- remote assets are blocked by default in most clients. Canela, the DPEG display face, is a licensed webfont and cannot be loaded, so the wordmark and headline fall back to Georgia/Times to stay in the serif register. (3) border-radius degrades to square corners in Outlook desktop -- accepted. (4) The hidden preheader div uses mso-hide:all, which linters flag as an unknown property -- expected, do not 'fix'. (5) SIZE IS A HARD CONSTRAINT: this file is base64-embedded into an ANONYMOUS Apex script capped at ~32,000 characters TOTAL across all three blobs plus the script's own code. The loader was restructured to loop over a definition list rather than repeat a block per template specifically to make three templates fit; it currently sits at ~22,500 characters. Check the script length after regenerating any blob.
_brand_palette: Taken from the live dhananipeg.com CSS bundle (theme custom properties), not eyeballed: --color-primary #0e3416 (header bar, headline, emphasis), --color-accent #4db892 (rule under the header, eyebrow label, callout left border), --color-footer #0a2a12 (footer bar), --color-surface-green #edf2ec (callout background), --color-surface-warm #f5f7f2 (page background). Note this is deep forest green -- the earlier IR templates used #B85D0D orange, which was never a DPEG brand colour.
_org_copy_can_be_clobbered_by_the_builde: Same risk as the sibling templates: opening an SFX template in Setup's Email Template Builder and saving REGENERATES HtmlValue from the Builder canvas, discarding whatever the loader wrote. Because Markup (the canvas) is not writable via DML for TemplateType='custom', the loader cannot pre-populate the canvas to protect against this. OPERATIONAL RULE: edit this template by changing the .html here and re-running the loader -- never by opening it in Email Template Builder.
_Markup_and_IsBuilderContent_NOT_INCLUDE: Same platform restrictions measured for the sibling templates apply identically: Markup can only be set via DML for TemplateType='visualforce' (this is 'custom'), and IsBuilderContent is createable=false/updateable=false under all circumstances. Neither field is set by the loader. See IR_Lead_Notification_Email.json for the full measured writeup.
_why_a_plain_send_email_action_is_not_us: MEASURED 2026-09-11 against this org, in order. (1) emailSimple with emailBody + recipientId fails outright: CANNOT_EXECUTE_FLOW_TRIGGER, '0 recipients' -- recipientId resolves an address only on the emailTemplateId path, and because a record-triggered flow error aborts the save, this also blocked Offering creation entirely until it was fixed. (2) emailSimple with emailBody + emailAddresses delivers, but always as text/plain: the recipient sees raw markup. richTextFormattedBody=true on the action and isViewedAsPlainText=false on the Text Template were both verified present in the retrieved org copy, and the body was tried stored as CDATA and as escaped entities -- no effect. (3) emailSimple with emailTemplateId + recipientId renders HTML correctly, but the template cannot then merge the triggering Offering's fields, because relatedRecordId is rejected alongside a User recipientId ('WhatId is not available for sending emails to UserIds', HTTP 400) -- the same restriction documented at length in IR_Lead_Notification_Email.json. So through emailSimple, rendered HTML and the Offering name are mutually exclusive. Messaging.SingleEmailMessage.setHtmlBody() has neither limitation, which is why OfferingEmailSender exists.
